title: Article prefixes with LEFT
objective: Use LEFT to take the first characters of an article code and feed the result into a lookup.
instructions: Each article code in column A starts with a two-letter category prefix and a six-character style code (for example SN-450). In B2:B7, extract the two-letter prefix with LEFT. In C2:C7, look the prefix in column B up in the category list in F1:G6 with XLOOKUP, showing the text "Unknown" when the prefix is not in the list. In D2:D7, extract the six-character style code with LEFT. Fix the category list with $ signs.
hints: LEFT(text, number_of_characters) returns characters from the start of the text. =LEFT(A2,2) gives the first two characters of A2.
The style code is the first six characters, so use LEFT(A2,6). For the category use =XLOOKUP(B2,$F$2:$F$6,$G$2:$G$6,"Unknown").
Matching ignores upper and lower case, so bt in a lower-case code still finds BT in the list. A prefix that is not in the list, like XX, returns the fourth argument.
